gaps.title: Confirmed breaches are not published
gaps.description: Only formal enforcement actions are published. Regulator findings of confirmed breach are not public in any jurisdiction, so a service can accumulate many confirmed breaches and still show a clean enforcement flag.

evidence.claim: Four Corners reported 320 confirmed breaches across one operator's NSW centres (Jan 2024 to Sep 2025) with zero infringement notices issued.
StartingBlocks shows six enforcement action types for the past two years, not breach findings.

open_questions: Does any state publish confirmed breach counts per service, even in aggregate?
What did the NSW parliamentary inquiry recommend on breach publication, and was it adopted in the October 2025 reforms?
gaps.next_action: register-auditor: confirm per jurisdiction whether confirmed breaches are published in any form.

gaps.title: No joined national enforcement picture
gaps.description: Enforcement actions are published by eight jurisdictions plus the Commonwealth in incompatible formats (NSW quarterly PDFs, Victorian monthly HTML pages, others), with no national join on the service approval number.

evidence.claim: NSW publishes a register of enforcement actions as quarterly PDFs.
Victoria (VECRA) publishes enforcement actions as monthly HTML pages.

open_questions: Do all registers carry the SE-/PR- approval numbers needed for a clean join?
What are the licence terms on each state register?
gaps.next_action: register-auditor: build the per-jurisdiction format, key and licence matrix.

gaps.title: No public ownership graph
gaps.description: StartingBlocks links services to their approved provider, but not approved providers to corporate groups, brands or owners across states and over time.

evidence.claim: StartingBlocks added provider-linked services in September 2025; corporate group ownership is not shown.

open_questions: Do ACECQA provider records include ABN or ACN?
Can ASIC company relationships be obtained under an open licence without paid extracts?
gaps.next_action: register-auditor: check ABN presence in the ACECQA provider register and ABR/ASIC licence terms.

gaps.title: Services outside the NQF have no public list
gaps.description: Four Corners reported 473 services operating outside the National Quality Framework, with no public list of which services they are or which instrument regulates each.

evidence.claim: 473 services operate outside the NQF; 142 are to be brought in.
Queensland publishes a licence register for non-NQF services as CSV.

open_questions: Confirm 473 and 142 against the education ministers' communique.
Where do other states list their non-NQF services?
gaps.next_action: source-researcher: find the official source for 473 and 142.

gaps.title: No per-service history
gaps.description: Ratings, conditions and enforcement flags are published as current state, and enforcement actions drop off StartingBlocks after two years. No public per-service history exists.

evidence.claim: StartingBlocks enforcement display covers actions issued in the past two years.

open_questions: Does ACECQA publish per-service historical ratings anywhere, including in NQF Snapshot data files?
gaps.next_action: register-auditor: inspect NQF Snapshot data files for per-service history.

gaps.title: Rating age is not surfaced as a risk signal
gaps.description: StartingBlocks shows the last regulator visit date but not how old the rating is relative to the sector, so an old rating looks as strong as a recent one.

evidence.claim: StartingBlocks added the last regulatory authority visit date in September 2025.

open_questions: What is the distribution of time since last assessment, by state? Is it derivable from the national register?
gaps.next_action: register-auditor: confirm the national register includes the rating issued date.

gaps.title: Serious incident data is aggregate only
gaps.description: Serious incident rates are published nationally (160 per 100 services in 2024-25) but never per service or by provider type, so the for-profit versus not-for-profit claim cannot be tested from public data.

evidence.claim: Serious incidents rose to 160 per 100 services in 2024-25.

open_questions: Has any regulator published serious incidents by provider management type?
gaps.next_action: source-researcher: check the 2025 NQF Annual Performance Report tables.
